blocks.text: The unnamed disciple “whom Jesus loved” is presented as an authoritative witness, but the Gospel itself never identifies him as John son of Zebedee; John 21:24 also refers to this disciple in the third person. The footwashing has therefore been read in several ways—as an enactment of Jesus’ love and service, as connected with cleansing, and as a pattern for disciples. These readings do not authorize leadership that humiliates or coerces others.

Jesus calls love for one another a “new commandment,” yet closely related Johannine writings describe this commandment both as received from the beginning and as something actively urged. Its relationship to Jesus tradition is close, but the direction of literary dependence among these writings remains disputed.
